page: Microsoft Azure EC16eds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance deployed on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The system is driven by an x86_64 Intel processor architecture providing 16 dedicated vCPUs. It is configured with 128.0 GB of total RAM, which translates to a high memory density of 8.0 GB per vCPU core.

For local disk operations, the instance is equipped with 944 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage and supports Azure Premium Storage for external managed disk attachments. It does not include discrete GPUs and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, directing host capabilities strictly toward CPU, memory, and local I/O performance.

The 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio coupled with bundled local NVMe storage provides qualitative resource efficiency for memory-heavy and disk-caching tasks without the need to over-provision compute cores. A key architectural tradeoff is the absence of GPU acceleration, which excludes machine learning training or parallel graphical computation.

This server type is primarily structured for memory-intensive workloads, including large relational database systems, in-memory caching solutions, enterprise resource planning applications, and distributed analytics engines requiring fast local scratch disks.

The instance contains zero GPUs, focusing physical host resources strictly on general CPU and memory throughput. Operating without complimentary public IPv4 addresses, the configuration is structured for internal cluster environments or workloads behind dedicated network gateways. The EC16eds_v6 is well-suited for high-throughput enterprise databases, in-memory key-value stores, distributed analytics nodes, and transactional processing engines requiring high memory density alongside integrated solid-state storage.
